dialogue.content: （こんにちは。本日は宜しくお願いします！お時間になりましたら、始めさせて頂きます。）
dialogue.English: (Hello. I'm looking forward to our session today. We'll get started at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: （こんにちは。よろしくお願いいたします。）
dialogue.English: (Hello. I'm looking forward to it as well.)

dialogue.content: 本日はご相談にお越しいただき、ありがとうございます。よろしければ、あなたの年齢、性別をお聞かせ頂けますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in for counseling today. If you don't mind, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: 15歳、女子です
dialogue.English: I'm a 15-year-old girl.

dialogue.content: お答えいただき、ありがとうございます。本日は、どのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. What brings you here today?

dialogue.content: なんか、ハブられてて、、つらいです
dialogue.English: I’m kind of being left out… it’s really hard.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね…それはつらいですよね…もう少し詳しく状況を教えてもらってもいいですか？
dialogue.English: I see... That must be really tough... Could you tell me a bit more about what's been going on?

dialogue.content: 話しかけてもスルーされるし、LINEも既読スルーされるし、もうイヤです
dialogue.English: When I talk to them, they ignore me, and on LINE they leave my messages on read. I’m just fed up.

dialogue.content: そうなんだ…つらいよね…スルーしてくるのは誰なのか教えてくれますか？
dialogue.English: I see... that must be painful. Could you tell me who is ignoring you?

dialogue.content: みんなです
dialogue.English: Everyone.

dialogue.content: もう死にたい
dialogue.English: I just want to die.

dialogue.content: そっか…そんな辛い状況なのに、よく相談してくれたね、ありがとう。
dialogue.English: I hear you... Thank you for having the courage to talk about this, especially when things are so difficult.

dialogue.content: みんなっていうのは、学校のクラスのみんなかな？
dialogue.English: By "everyone," do you mean your classmates at school?

dialogue.content: そうです
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね…いつからそうなったのかな？
dialogue.English: I see... When did this start happening?

dialogue.content: 前からなんとなく、冷たくなったなって思ってたけど、クラス替えしてから急激にひどくなりました
dialogue.English: I'd felt for a while that they were getting colder towards me, but it got drastically worse after our classes were changed.

dialogue.content: そうなんだ…それは辛いよね…クラス替えをしてひどくなった理由は、何なのかな？
dialogue.English: I see… that must be hard. Do you have any sense of why it got worse after the class change?

dialogue.content: わかりません。私何もしてないのに、、、どうしたらいいですか？
dialogue.English: I don't know. I haven't done anything... What should I do?

dialogue.content: そうだよね…このことは誰か周りに相談できそうな人はいるかな？
dialogue.English: I understand... Is there anyone around you that you feel you could talk to about this?

dialogue.content: いません
dialogue.English: No one.

dialogue.content: Twitterのウラ垢でツイートしたら、わかるよって言ってくれた人はいるけど、、
dialogue.English: There was someone who replied to my tweet on my secret Twitter account saying they understand, but...

dialogue.content: その人はどんな人なの？
dialogue.English: What kind of person are they?

dialogue.content: 大学2年生の男の人
dialogue.English: A guy who's a sophomore in college.

dialogue.content: その男の人はTwitterでやりとりしている人なの？
dialogue.English: Is this man someone you interact with on Twitter?

dialogue.content: そうです
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね…ツイートしたら、わかるよっていうのはどういうことなのかな？
dialogue.English: I see... What did they mean by 'I understand' in response to your tweet?

dialogue.content: ハブられるのってつらいよねって、、
dialogue.English: They said that being left out is really hard...

dialogue.content: なるほど…つらさをわかってくれる人がいたんだね
dialogue.English: I see... so you found someone who understands your pain.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: なんでも相談に乗るよって言ってくれます
dialogue.English: He says I can talk to him about anything.

dialogue.content: うんうん…Twitterの裏垢みたいな本音を家族や周りの人に、話してみたことはある？
dialogue.English: I see... Have you ever tried talking about your true feelings, like the ones you post on your secret Twitter account, with your family or people around you?

dialogue.content: まさか、、、ないです
dialogue.English: No way… I haven’t.

dialogue.content: ウラ垢の意味がなくなる、、
dialogue.English: That would defeat the purpose of a secret account...

dialogue.content: 親には心配かけたくないです
dialogue.English: I don’t want to worry my parents.

dialogue.content: そっか…心配かけたくないんだね…親はどんな人なの？
dialogue.English: I see... so you don't want to worry them. What are your parents like?

dialogue.content: あなたのことをなんてお呼びしたら、いいかな？ニックネームでもいいので、教えてくださるとうれしいです。
dialogue.English: What would you like me to call you? A nickname is fine; I'd be happy if you could tell me.

dialogue.content: 春香です
dialogue.English: I’m Haruka.

dialogue.content: 親は厳しいです
dialogue.English: My parents are strict.

dialogue.content: 明日から学校行くと思うと死にたくなる、、
dialogue.English: The thought of going to school tomorrow makes me want to die...

dialogue.content: 春香さんだね、ありがとう。どんなところが厳しいの？
dialogue.English: Haruka, thank you. In what ways are they strict?

dialogue.content: 真面目な両親で、勉強にも厳しくて、だから進学校に入れられました
dialogue.English: My parents are very serious and strict about my studies, so they sent me to a college prep school.

dialogue.content: そうだったんだね…
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: 必ずしも学校に行かないといけないと訳ではないよ辛かったから休んでもいいんだよ
dialogue.English: You don't necessarily have to go to school. If it's too painful, it's okay to take a break.

dialogue.content: 親が許してくれないと思う
dialogue.English: I don't think my parents would allow it.

dialogue.content: そっか…けど春香さんが辛いことをまだ親御さんに話してないから、どんな反応が返ってくるかわからないと思わない？
dialogue.English: I understand... But since you haven't told your parents yet how painful this is for you, you don't really know how they'll react, do you?

dialogue.content: そうかもしれないけど、、LINEのこととか言ったら、スマホ取り上げられるかも、、、
dialogue.English: That might be true, but... if I tell them about the LINE messages, they might take away my phone...

dialogue.content: そうだね…それは心配かもしれないけど、春香さんが辛い思いをしているのに、一方的にスマホを取り上げたりはしないと思うけど、どうかな？
dialogue.English: I understand... That's a valid concern, but I don't think they would just take away your phone when you're going through such a painful time. What do you think?

dialogue.content: わかりません。物理的にいじめられてるわけじゃないし、気にするなって言われそう、、スマホ持ってるから余計なこと気になるんだって前から言われてるし、、
dialogue.English: I’m not sure. It’s not like I’m being physically bullied, so they might say, “Don’t let it bother you.” They’ve told me before that having a smartphone just makes me worry about unnecessary things…

dialogue.content: 死にたくなるほど、辛いのは立派ないじめだから、春香さんは助けを求めていいんだよ
dialogue.English: Feeling so much pain that you want to die is definitely a form of bullying, so it's okay for you to ask for help, Haruka.

dialogue.content: たとえば家族のなかで一番、話やすいのは誰かな？
dialogue.English: For example, who in your family is the easiest to talk to?

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。。
dialogue.English: Oh, I see...

dialogue.content: お母さんかな
dialogue.English: My mom, I guess.

dialogue.content: でも怖い
dialogue.English: But I’m scared.

dialogue.content: うんうん…怖いよね…
dialogue.English: Yes... I understand it's scary...

dialogue.content: 親に心配かけたくないっていう、気持ちはとても優しく素晴らしいことだけど、ここに勇気を出して相談にきてくれたんだから、きっとお母さんにも話せるよ
dialogue.English: Not wanting to worry your parents is a very kind and wonderful feeling, but you had the courage to come here and talk about it, so I'm sure you can talk to your mother, too.

dialogue.content: うーん、考えてみます
dialogue.English: Hmm, I’ll think about it.

dialogue.content: ではお母さんにどんな風に伝えればいいか、ここで一緒に考えてみませんか？
dialogue.English: Then, would you like to think together here about how you could tell your mother?

dialogue.content: はい、お願いします
dialogue.English: Yes, please.

dialogue.content: お母さんは厳しいって言ってたけど、春香さんはお母さんの優しいところもたくさん知っていると思うんだけど、どうかな？
dialogue.English: You said your mother is strict, but I imagine you also know many of her kind sides, Haruka. What do you think?

dialogue.content: そうですね。。小さい時はもっと優しかったかな、、、
dialogue.English: That's true... I think she was kinder when I was little...

dialogue.content: うんうん…きっと成長と共に親との会話がぎくしゃくしちゃうことってよくあることだよ会話のコミュニケーションって、伝え方がポイントなんだよ
dialogue.English: Yes... It's very common for conversations with parents to become a bit awkward as you grow up. The key to communication is how you express yourself.

dialogue.content: 勉強に厳しいのは、春香さんのことをお母さんが大切に思ってくれているからだと思うんだ
dialogue.English: I think she's strict about studies because she cares deeply about you, Haruka.

dialogue.content: だから、学校に行きたくない、ってことだけを伝えるんじゃなくて、少しずつ、こんなことがあって辛いんだ、って気持ちを伝えてみるの
dialogue.English: So, instead of just saying, 'I don't want to go to school,' try to gradually convey your feelings, like, 'This happened, and it's really painful for me.'

dialogue.content: いきなりすべてを話すのはハードルが高いかもしれないから、前から冷たい態度を取られてたけどクラス替えをして、いじめがひどくなって辛くなったことから、少しずつ話してみるのはどうかな？
dialogue.English: It might be too difficult to tell her everything at once, so how about starting little by little? You could begin by explaining that people were already being cold to you, but the bullying got worse and became very painful after the classes were changed.

dialogue.content: そうですね、、、話せるかな、、、勉強に厳しいのは、親戚もみんな優秀で、高学歴で、姉も現役で京大に入ってて、私も同じように優秀で当たり前だって言われています。だから成績も常にトップじゃなきゃ意味がないって、、、
dialogue.English: Right... I wonder if I can... The reason they're so strict about my studies is that all my relatives are high-achievers with good educations. My older sister got into Kyoto University right out of high school, and they say it's only natural for me to be just as successful. That's why they say my grades are meaningless unless I'm always at the top...

dialogue.content: クラスのことなんとなく話した時も、そんなこと気にしてないで、勉強に集中しなさいって言われて、、、
dialogue.English: When I vaguely mentioned what was happening in class once, they told me not to worry about things like that and to just focus on my studies...

dialogue.content: そっか…常に成績トップを目指すなんてしんどいよね
dialogue.English: I see... It must be exhausting to always have to aim for the top grades.

dialogue.content: なんとなく話すことはできたんだね…きっとお母さんは春香さんが死にたいほど、辛いことを知らなかったからじゃないかな
dialogue.English: So you were able to mention it vaguely... Maybe it's just that your mother didn't know you were in so much pain that you were thinking of dying.

dialogue.content: そうですね、、、怖いから、友達の話みたいにしました、、
dialogue.English: That's true... I was scared, so I talked about it as if it were happening to a friend...

dialogue.content: うんうん…そっか…言葉で伝えないとわからないことって、たくさんあると思うんだ他人を見ただけ、この人、今、こんな気持ちだ！なんてなかなかわからないものだよね…
dialogue.English: Yes... I see... I think there are many things people can't understand unless you put them into words. It's hard to just look at someone and know exactly what they're feeling, right?

dialogue.content: 親子も人間関係だから、なかなか以心伝心は難しいと思うんだだから春香さんの気持ちをお母さんに伝えてあげてほしい
dialogue.English: The parent-child relationship is still a human relationship, so I think it's difficult to understand each other without words. That's why I really hope you can tell your mother how you feel, Haruka.

dialogue.content: うまく伝えられるかわからないけど、できるだけ話してみようと思います
dialogue.English: I don't know if I can explain it well, but I'll try my best to talk to her.

dialogue.content: うん！こうやってここに勇気を出して相談に来てくれた春香さんなら、きっと話せると思うよ
dialogue.English: Yes! A person like you, Haruka, who had the courage to come here and talk, can definitely do it.

dialogue.content: その勇気を持って、自分で自分を助けてあげるってすごく大事なことあとはもちろん、周りの人に助けてもらうことも大切だから、お母さんに気持ちを伝えてみてね
dialogue.English: Having that courage and helping yourself is a very important thing. And of course, it's also important to get help from others, so please try telling your mother how you feel.

dialogue.content: はい、わかりました
dialogue.English: Okay, I will.

dialogue.content: うん、きっとできるよ！
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm sure you can do it!

dialogue.content: もう少しお話したいところでだけど、そろそろお時間になってしまいましたね。今日の相談はこれで、終わりになるけどいいかな？
dialogue.English: I'd like to talk more, but it looks like our time is almost up. Is it okay if we end today's session here?

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: またいつでも相談にきてくださいね今日は相談してくれてありがとう！
dialogue.English: Please feel free to come back and talk anytime. Thank you for opening up to me today!

dialogue.content: （本日はありがとうございました！とても勉強になりました。忌憚のないフィードバックをよろしくお願いいたします！）
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much for today! It was a great learning experience. I would appreciate your candid feedback!)

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you.)

dialogue.content: （それでは終了いたします）
dialogue.English: (I will now end the session.)
